c.tagline: Japan's cosmopolitan port city of marbled beef, mountain views, and old foreign quarters.

taxi.fareNote: Metered; ride-hailing is limited in Japan - apps like GO, DiDi and Uber dispatch licensed taxis rather than private drivers, and there is no informal street bargaining.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the police; 119 is for fire and ambulance.

avoid.reason: Minor bar-tout hustle in the Sannomiya nightlife district late at night.

hood_desc: Kobe's downtown transport hub and main shopping-and-eating district, where JR, Hankyu, Hanshin, subway, and Port Liner lines all meet; covered arcades, department stores, and izakaya make it the obvious base.

The hillside quarter of Kitano-cho, lined with the Ijinkan - the Western-style mansions of 19th-century foreign traders, such as the Weathercock House - now home to cafes, boutiques, and viewpoints over the city.
A long shopping arcade rolling down to Nankinmachi, Kobe's compact, lantern-strung Chinatown packed with street-food stalls and dim sum; the city's liveliest place to browse and graze.
Kobe's redeveloped waterfront of the red Port Tower, the Maritime Museum, a Ferris wheel, and the umie mall; a breezy, illuminated place for a harbourside evening out.

An eastern district famous as one of Japan's great sake-brewing regions, with historic breweries and tasting halls along the coast, plus the ferries and stadium at nearby Rokko Island; quieter and residential.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink everywhere.

transit.hours: Subways and trains run roughly 5:30am to just past midnight, with no regular overnight service; night buses and taxis fill the gap after the last trains.
transit.note: Kobe is stitched together by JR and the private Hankyu and Hanshin lines, the Kobe Municipal Subway (Seishin-Yamate and Kaigan lines), and the automated Port Liner linking Sannomiya to Port Island and the airport; the retro City Loop and Port Loop buses connect the main sights.
transit.pay: Buy an ICOCA or PiTaPa IC card from station machines and tap in and out, or tap a contactless card at some gates; subway base fares start around ¥210 (~$1.40) and rise with distance. Day passes cover the tourist loop buses.

transit.m: Kobe-Kanku Bay Shuttle ferry from Kansai Airport (~30 min)
